These techniques result in textural effects and moods that range from aged and distressed to vibrant and energetic. Through layering the imagery and combining the collage components, I explore how color, form, and movement interact compositionally.

medium: Encaustic pigmented beeswax using a shellac technique for texture with paper collage on wood panel
description: Three fish, trapped in an eddy, crusted with coral-white lace and tarnished sediment. I wanted the cracked, bubbled textures to feel like tide pools and shipwreck remains — life surviving quietly under weathered surfaces. Subject and relic both, worn down by the same slow erosion.

title: A Walk in the Woods
description: For this piece, the gentle blending and soft colors of watercolor pencils allowed me to create a dreamy woodland scene that reflects my appreciation of nature as a place of beauty, mystery and peace.

artist_bio: Helen Hankin is a mixed media artist.
title: WILDFIRE
medium: Mixed media: Fluid acrylics on paper with collage
description: This painting captures a moment in time where beautiful lush undergrowth in a forest is facing an approaching wild fire. Reflects this artists concern for the devastation of precious vegetation, tress, creatures from increasing wildfires related to climate change. Also the great consequences for human health and the environment.

artist_bio: Malini Rao is a Boston-based oil painter working in a cubist-inspired visual language. Her work sits at the intersection of structure and intuition—building geometric frameworks around warm, organic subjects with colors mixed directly on the canvas. Shifting between brush and palette knife, she tests her style across cultural themes, sensory experience, and portraiture. Every piece is both a construction and a discovery—geometry provides the architecture, while intuition determines what survives within it.
title: The Ghat
description: The Ghat is the first painting in a three-part series exploring Varanasi, a city I have never visited yet one that has lived vividly in my imagination for most of my life. I returned to oils after nearly two decades away, and it was Varanasi that called first. Not as a subject I chose deliberately, but as something that was simply waiting. This painting holds the widest frame of the series. The Ganges at dawn: abstract, serene, expansive. Humanity is barely a whisper on the water and the morning mist. There is breath here, and stillness. That stolen hour when the river still belongs to the birds, to murmured ablutions, to prayers rising before the ghats fill and the day arrives with its beautiful, relentless chaos. Man is incidental for now. Serenity is the subject. I worked on this piece for close to a year, returning to it only at the close of each workday. Coming back to oils after two decades was a slow reacquainting: remembering what I had always loved about the medium, its weight, the way it moves and holds, the way it rewards patience over urgency. My cubist-inspired visual language, with its geometric overlays and angular structures, finds an unusual quiet here. The geometry doesn't impose itself on the scene so much as hold space for it, tracing the invisible structure beneath stillness itself. The Ghat was the beginning of a conversation. Between who I was and who I was becoming. Between a city I carry inside me and the canvas that was finally ready to hold it.

artist_bio: My recent work emerges from a space where grief, memory and rebirth converge. I now approach each piece as an act of both mourning and celebration - honoring the lives that shaped me, the one's I've lost and the new one I hold close.
title: Fragments No.13
medium: Mixed media: Acrylic, spray-paint, cardboard, staples, screen patch, vintage boxes, photograph, grass cloth wallpaper, recycled envelopes, book binding
description: Fragments of paper, fabric, and memory are stapled into a quiet narrative of time and touch. At this moment, layers reveal histories both personal and anonymous, balancing fragility and structure. The work invites slow looking, where texture, repair, and absence become language, holding traces of lives and those forgotten.

medium: Sumi inks on kozo paper, collage, chalk and cold wax, on wood panel.
description: I’m interested in how landscapes hold traces of everything that’s passed through them, the way memory does. I painted a landscape resembling ash and bone, layered with memory and torn textures. Asemic writing, a lone sentinel, and a red-eyed sun sit off in the distance.

title: See You Tonight
description: My paintings explore the use of mixed media and oil paint to capture the fleeting nature of time and how the changes of light alter the emotion one may feel when effected by that light. I've created textured spaces that invite viewers to pause and reflect.

artist_bio: Artist, writer, and orchardist Linda Hoffman, lives at Old Frog Pond Farm in Harvard, MA, where she curates the farm’s annual outdoor sculpture exhibit, now in its 20th year. Her art includes indoor and outdoor sculpture, public installations, private commissions, and painting. She often uses natural materials  in her sculpture and explores themes of climate change and the spiritual journey. She is the author of The Artist and the Orchard: A Memoir.
title: Portal
medium: Watercolor, bronze bust, found metal, wood, old nails
description: Where is the present found? In the landscape, the viewer, or the act of seeing? A rusted iron ring becomes a portal rather than a boundary. A small bronze abstract figure invites us to discover how each moment opens into another.

artist_bio: Kate Derosier spent a lot of time and effort trying not to be an artist – even completing an entire Ph.D. in neuroscience. After taking time off work to have kids, she realized that what she missed wasn’t science, but the creative work she had been telling herself could only ever be a hobby.  Since then, she has been focusing on painting, using classes and self-study to grow beyond the fundamentals  learned in college.
title: Battery Townsley
description: This painting is based on photos and memories from a hike in the Marin Headlands. There are lots of these abandoned WWII-era military structures that hiding along the California coast. Visiting this one with my friends was one really nice day during a difficult time for me.

artist_bio: I typically work in acrylic on canvas, board, or paper. For years I have explored the idea of several points of view inhabiting the same space.
title: Manifestation
description: A theme I enjoy is form manifesting / differentiating from the field. Calligraphic mark figures prominently in my work and for me has meaning as word/sound/vibration. My work is inspired by joy, light, and an exploration of consciousness.

artist_bio: Christiane Corcelle’s work is guided by curiosity and a drive to explore materials, processes, and ideas. Her multi-disciplinary practice embraces painting, printmaking, collage, and installation, allowing her to move fluidly across mediums and techniques. This openness results in a body of work that is versatile, evocative, and alive with discovery. Through her art, Corcelle seeks new perspectives, revealing beauty and meaning in unexpected places.
title: The Day The Fish Arrived
image: Corcelle C_The Day The Fish Arrived_1.jpg
description: Built with layers of collage and paint, this piece grew one step at a time. Bright fish appear as unexpected visitors, bringing color, joy, and a sense of wonder. It reminds us that ordinary moments can become something special.

artist_bio: Vicki Kocher Paret currently lives and paints in Cambridge. She is a representational painter, exploring beauty in objects and place. Her formal training began with a BFA in Painting and Printmaking from Virginia Commonwealth University, and later she completed her Master of Arts in Teaching in Art Education at Tufts University/School of the Museum of Fine Arts Boston. She is currently represented by Galatea Fine Arts in SoWA Boston.

title: Iceflown
description: Even as the landscape changes, memory is held within natural cycles; there is a lot of work and life happening beneath the surface. As ice melts, it marks time and, through its changes, is reflective of how the world is evolving and suffering.

artist_bio: Rose Walsh-Cooke is a representational painter, originally from the UK. She has lived in New England for over 25 years and paints local landscapes and seascapes in an impressionistic style. Known for using thick, buttery, expressive paint, her work has been described as using "a direct painterly approach achieving loose precision." She has exhibited locally, including solo shows in Lexington and Concord, MA. She has also shown her work at Galaray House Art Gallery in SoWa Boston and the Molly Nye Gallery at LexArt.
title: In Flight
description: This is abstracted view of the fields encountered when flying in to the UK. It's the "moment" when I realize I'm entering Europe. This patchwork of greens always reminds me of where I came from.

artist_bio: Nature inspires me, and I am drawn to paint what I see there. My eyes bask in the colors while I analyze the forms that hold them.  I still try to control dye with resists to recreate what I see, but these methods are no longer my “go tos.” I no longer rush to fix breaks in my lines. I now know that in nature as in life, something beautiful may happen if I stand aside and let the colors play.
title: Cuba III
description: When visiting a botanical garden in Cuba, I photographed this fabulous monstera plant knowing that I would render it in dye on silk.  I enjoyed creating the various textures by letting water and alcohol play with the dye.

artist_bio: Heidi Mann is an oil painter based in Lexington, Massachusetts. A graduate of the Massachusetts College of Art, she began her creative career in the video game industry, where she worked for many years as a background painter and texture artist. This experience deeply informs her understanding of environment, atmosphere, and visual storytelling. Returning to her original passion for oil painting, Mann brings a heightened sensitivity to light, pattern, and composition.
title: Lamp
description: Eerie light in an old hotel.

description: Unfold reveals an inner world shaped by memory. Blurred moments intentionally mimic the ambiguity of remembrance, while textures of brushstrokes and palette knife marks reflect painting's unique ability to make memories and dreams tangible. Together, this piece unfolds the person we become through what we remember and imagine.

artist_bio: My work is about those moments when light reveals what is beautiful about ordinary places and things. I am generally attracted to run-down buildings, alleys glimpsed in passing, or the way light caresses moldings on an old house. Somehow, in the spaces between light and shadow, I see reflections of the people who inhabit or built the structures: a hint of the human condition.
title: The Motel Room
description: The painting is of a typical motel room in Truro. Motel rooms hold mysteries: is it an escape, a place to reunite, a symbol of renewal?

artist_bio: My recent work is suggestive of new or previously hidden views, sometimes seen through transitory glimpses of light, reflection or the prism of water. These views suggest dimensions beyond which we can normally see; glimpses that may appear without warning, whether sudden and clear, or effuse and transient as mist. This work points toward hope, and an opening of mind to evoke solution.

description: This piece is inspired by Leonard Cohen's poem/song. I build a structural unity that is intended as present while seeming to be simultaneously evolving. Edges of the underlying images are an integral part of the work, evoking the unity of parts coming together, and dissolving or evolving forms.

artist_bio: Mary Rose O’Connell is best known for her dynamic oil paintings of the New England coast. Other genres she has mastered are her sensitive portrait, still life, and landscape paintings. She paints in her studio and en plein air in a representational style. Classically trained in the Boston School Tradition, her work shows a strong grounding in composition and design combined with the color and light of the 19th century Impressionists.
title: Breaking Surf
medium: Oil paint on oil primed cradled board.
description: The new England coast offers continued inspiration. This painting was created using plein air studies in oil and gouache along with photos when I returned to work in the studio.

artist_bio: C. J. Lori is an oil painter living in Brookline, Massachusetts. Her work reflects her interest in literature, anthropology and psychology, as well as an abiding fascination with the natural world. Often called “Neo-surrealism” or “magic realism,” Ms. Lori’s paintings explore the complex relationship between humanity and the environment. She exaggerates or distorts color, form and composition to emphasize sensations that are often contradictory: clarity and mystery, excitement and sorrow, beauty and decay.
title: Loch Leaving
description: “Loch Leaving” was inspired by a recent trip to Scotland. It was unusual weather for Scotland, very dry and sunny with waterfalls reduced to trickles. The gear I packed for their notorious weather never left my suitcase, and I pondered the impact of climate change on Scotland’s exquisite landscape.

artist_bio: Trying to find the color of light is something that I have pursued in my paintings for years, no matter what the subject matter of that period. I am fascinated by the way the color reflected on a person or thing is altered depending on the light and the environment
title: A Moment's Gesture
description: With the figure in water, there is much to explore; the color of light, reflection, and distortion as well as a gesture that relates to a sense of place and moment. My pool paintings also enable me to explore a subject that gives me peace in these turbulent times.

title: Cape Cod Sunset
description: I enjoy painting and experimenting with color. My preferred subjects are related to nature and the outdoors. Painting has taught me to see things in a different way, observing every detail more carefully and more consciously, distinguishing colors and shapes, and ultimately appreciating more deeply what I see.

artist_bio: I am primarily a realist, which for me means trying to reflect the beauty of this world God created. I work to capture the light and 3-dimensional volume of my subject. My work is also known for its colorful and textural qualities. I love color! I will take on almost any subject which appeals to me… including but not limited to landscape, architecture, still life, animals and people.
title: On Bass Rocks
description: The sea meets the craggy shore at Bass Rocks in Gloucester. In the distance a few venerable old homes dot the coast. An artist pulls the blue and white in from the sea.

artist_bio: Jin is an artist in the greater Boston area with a passion for painting and a background in graphic design. She enjoys working with vibrant colors in acrylic, gouache, collage and mixed media. Living in New England, she is influenced by the changes of the seasons, diverse landscape, and flora and strives to draw attention to the beauty of everyday moments.
title: Hemlock Haven
description: My work explores the intersections of color theory and the natural world by using gouache to examine how shifting hues alter human emotion and perception. Using gouache I isolate specific color relationships, mirroring both the delicate balances found in the environment and my own internal emotional state.

artist_bio: I am a Boston-area artist who works with encaustic paint — a mixture of beeswax, damar resin, and pigment that is applied in layers and fused with heat. My multi-layer paintings are studies in color, composition, and texture that highlight the unique properties of the medium, and which are informed by my background in both fine arts and graphic design.
title: Ebb Tide
description: Using only horizontal bands of varying widths and textures, Hilary challenges herself to create a sense of space and distance while pushing her subject to the edge of abstraction. She has painted over a hundred seascapes in varying sizes and colors—they provide a consistent design framework with endless possibilities.

artist_bio: My oil paintings originate from photographs. I look for scenes that are not typically regarded as beautiful and figures experiencing the mundane “in between” moments. The compositions often incorporate wide-angle views, contrasting colors, and unusual viewpoints. Photoshop is my sketchpad as I digitally manipulate and adjust color combinations. I use my newly altered image as a reference as I paint. My intent is to make the viewer rethink our common, everyday scenes/objects.
title: Resettled
description: Immigrants integrate their past with the now.

title: Sedona Studio
medium: Mixed media: Photograph (taken by the artist), watercolor, stoneware clay, plastic plant
description: A trip to Sedona yielded this 3 medium work. The photograph is of formations in Sedona. The scene is a fictional studio overlooking the formations.

title: High Plains
description: Inspired by Maynard Dixon I took a trip to the Southwest. Watercolor and a  faux wood frame constructed out clay seemed like a good mash-up on mediums to me.

I studied Drawing, Painting, Sculpture, and Printmaking at Boston University, and Graphic Design and Illustration at U.C.Berkeley Extension in San Francisco. My work is in many private collections and has been featured in national publications and solo and group shows in Greater Boston, and New York City.
title: WATERHEAD MILL
description: A brick building façade punctuated by a variety of windows in different colors and styles, each revealing a unique character. The brick-red tones contrast with vibrant blues and soft pastels, creating interplay of structure and whimsy. Subtle textures and layered details invite closer inspection, offering a glimpse into urban life.

artist_bio: A Jordanian self-taught artist whose work is inspired by her own quest for spiritual enlightenment. Born in 1975 in Amman, Jordan, Tala Abu Nuwar who after a spiritual awakening decided to leave her corporate job to follow her dream of becoming the artist she feels she was meant to be.
title: She Tribe 2026
description: I am fascinated by the mystic world of Sufism.  I have a passion for mixing mysticism, Arabic poetry, yoga and the enchanting Sufi world of Rumi.  My goal is to awaken my heart and inspire others to close the eye of the self and awaken the eye of the soul.
